Find the arc length $L$ of the polar curve $r=3+3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{3}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above). Do not round the answer.

*Hint: You may wish to use the following identity: $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}.$*

$L=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=3+3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{(3+3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{9+18\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +9{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +9{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /3i}\sqrt{18+18\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{18}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we recall the identity for $\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2}):$

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{x}{2})=\sqrt{\frac{1+\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{2}}
$$

Therefore, using $x=\theta $ in the previous identity, the integral can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =3\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\sqrt{2{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =3\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={6\cdot 2(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2}))|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =12(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)) \\  & =12(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
